newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Trading subdued post FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Trading subdued post FOMC.

text.p: Corporate bond high-grade trading activity remained subdued and the high-yield market was similarly quiet despite the decision by Federal Reserve policy makers to keep interest rates steady, traders said.
"Everyone knew the Fed was going to stay on the sidelines, so it's been extremely, extremely quiet," one trader said.
Spreads were unchanged to a touch wider, high-grade players said.
"We've seen bank and finance paper widen one to two basis points because the 10 year Treasury is trading at a very rich 6.20 percent yield," another trader said.

Turning to the primary sector for high-grade issues no new names have circulated the market; however, with the yield on the T-bond approaching the critical 6.50 percent level issuers may be lured back in, dealers said.

"Most of this week's business is expected to come from the high-yield sector," said another syndicate player. "However, if the tone in the (Treasury) market improves this may spur some investment grade issuers to step in."
Currently, the benchmark 30-year bond is yielding 6.51 percent.
Although the FOMC was regarded as a nonevent by the market, syndicate players wanted the meeting out of the way before proceeding with any new business.
In the junk bond primary sector, about $2.2 billion in new supply is slated to come to market later in the week, syndicate players said.

Among this week's batch of new junk deals is Anaconda Nickel's $400 million private placement offering for its Murrin Murrin mining project in Western, Australia, players said. Natwest Capital Markets will underwrite the deal.
The deal is expected to include $300 million in 10-year senior secured fixed-rate notes and $100 million in nine-year senior secured floating-rate notes, sources said.
Another debt offering will come from Cablevision Systems Corp. The deal is expected to include $300 million 12-year 144a senior debentures via Bear Stearns and Merrill Lynch, sources said.

In the high-yield secondary arena, Grand Union bonds rose two points on after news on Tuesday that negotiations for a $75 million cash infusion to the struggling supermarket chain were underway, traders said.

"There are negotiations going on for financing," said Michael Sitrick, a spokesman for Shamrock Capital Advisors, who declined to comment on the amount, but said part of the proceeds would be used to cover the supermarket's September interest payment.
Sources close to the deal, however, said the loan would total $75 million.

Trefoil Capital Investors II LP, a Shamrock-managed investment vehicle for Roy E. Disney's family, and General Electric's GE Private Placement Partners II, agreed last year to purchase $100 million in Grand Union preferred stock. Grand Union stock closed at 1-7/8 on Tuesday.

In recent weeks, talk of a possible loan boosted Grand Union's bonds which had been trading sharply lower on rumors the company would default on a $39 million interest payment in September. Bonds rallied from the high 30's to the 50's over that time period, market sources said.

Grand Union 12 percent bonds ended higher on Tuesday at 51-1/2 bid, 52 offer, traders said. Among other issues, Iridium World Communications' debt gained 1-1/2 points, while Paging Network debt fell 3/4, traders said.
